{"type": "text", "text": "---\ntitle: What does a good trace look like?\nsidebarTitle: Best Practices\ndescription: Best practices for structuring Langfuse traces — scope, nesting, naming, input/output, and attributes — so that debugging, evaluation, and cost tracking work well.\n---\n\n# What does a good trace look like?\n\nYou see traces appearing in Langfuse, but how do you know if you've done it well? Here are a couple of things you can look at and optimize.\n\nTrace structure is not just cosmetic — many Langfuse features build on top of it:\n\n- [LLM-as-a-judge evaluators](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) target observations by name and type, and read their input and output.\n- [Dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards) filter and aggregate metrics by trace and observation names.\n- [Dataset experiments](/docs/evaluation/experiments) compare trace input and output across runs.\n- Saved views on the tracing table reference names and attributes.\n\nA well-structured trace makes debugging faster today, and stable names with meaningful input/output keep your evaluators, dashboards, and experiments working as your application evolves.\n\n## What's the scope of one trace?\n\nLangfuse's [data model](/docs/observability/data-model) has three levels of grouping: observations (individual steps) are grouped into traces via a `trace_id`, and traces can be grouped into sessions via a `session_id`.\n\nA trace represents one self-contained unit of work in your application. Good examples of a typical trace:\n\n- One chatbot turn (user sends a message, your app retrieves context, calls the LLM, returns a response)\n- One agent run (the agent receives a task, reasons, calls tools, and produces a result)\n- One pipeline execution (a document comes in, gets chunked, embedded, and stored)\n\nIf multiple of these happen in sequence, e.g. a multi-turn conversation, or several agent runs that feed into a final report, that's where [sessions](/docs/observability/features/sessions) come in. Each step is its own trace, and the session ties them together. For a chatbot this means one trace per turn and one session per conversation — you don't know upfront when a conversation ends, and the per-turn model keeps traces small and easy to navigate in the session view.\n\nA trace shows up in the Langfuse UI as a trace tree and an [agent graph](/docs/observability/features/agent-graphs):\n\n![Trace tree](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-tree.png)\n\n![Agent graph](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-agent-graph.png)\n\n## Look at the trace tree\n\nWhen you click on a trace, you see the trace tree. There are a few things you can check:\n\n### Are the right steps showing up?\n\nYou should see your LLM calls, tool calls, and other important steps represented in the tree. They should have the correct [observation type](/docs/observability/features/observation-types).\n\nFor example\n\n- an LLM call should show up as a `generation`. This is important because a `generation` can carry [cost, token usage, and model information](#track-model-tokens-and-cost-on-generations).\n- a tool call should show up as a `tool`. You can then filter on tool call observations when you create [LLM-as-a-judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) evaluators.\n\nFramework integrations typically set these types automatically. If you're instrumenting manually, you can set them via the `as_type` parameter (Python) or `asType` (JS/TS). See the [observation types docs](/docs/observability/features/observation-types) for a full list.\n\n### Is it nested correctly?\n\nA tool call should nest under the `agent` or `span` that orchestrates the step, as a sibling of the `generation` that requested it, so the tree shows which step each action belongs to instead of leaving tool calls dangling at the trace root.\n\nFramework integrations usually get this right automatically. If you're instrumenting manually, see [nesting observations](/docs/observability/sdk/instrumentation#nesting-observations).\n\n**Beware of aggregating LLM calls.** You should see a `generation` for each model invocation in an agent loop, interleaved with the `tool` calls it requested. Avoid wrapping the whole loop in one parent generation that only records the final output. This would make it impossible to:\n\n- see what the agent decided after each tool result\n- see which tool call has blown up your agent's context window (useful when optimizing cost)\n\n**One generation wrapping the whole loop.** You only see aggregated cost and the final output.\n\n![Agent loop collapsed into one generation](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-agent-collapsed-generation.png)\n\n**Each model invocation as its own generation.** You can see reasoning, tokens, cost after every step.\n\n![Agent loop with interleaved generations](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-agent-interleaved-generations.png)\n\n### Is there noise you don't need?\n\nNot every observation in the tree is useful for understanding what your application did. HTTP spans, database queries, and framework internals often add clutter without giving you meaningful insight. If you see observations like these polluting your trace tree, you can [filter them out](/faq/all/unwanted-http-database-spans).\n\n![Noisy spans in a trace tree](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-noisy-spans.png)\n\n## Choose good names\n\nObservation- and trace names are used in many places:\n\n- When setting up [LLM-as-a-judge evaluators](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge), you target specific observations by name.\n- In [dashboards](/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards), you can filter and aggregate metrics by observation name.\n- In the tracing table, names help you quickly identify what each step does.\n\nBecause names are referenced in all these places, treat them like an API: when a name changes, evaluators, dashboard queries, and saved filters that target the old name silently stop matching. Pick names deliberately, and expect to keep them stable.\n\n**Use active language.** Name observations after the action they perform, verb first: `classify-intent`, `retrieve-context`, `generate-response`, `summarize-results`. This makes the trace tree read like a description of what your application did, and makes filtering on a specific step easier.\n\n**Keep dynamic values out of names.** Use `process-order`, not `process-order-8945` or `generate-response-retry-2`. A name should identify the operation, not a single execution of it — otherwise every trace produces new names and you can no longer group, filter, or target them. Put run-specific values in [metadata](/docs/observability/features/metadata) instead. (This is the same low-cardinality rule that OpenTelemetry recommends for span names.)\n\nTry not to name observations after the AI model used (`gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet`). All filters, evaluators, and dashboards that reference the name break as soon as you swap models. The model is already a separate attribute on `generation` observations, use that instead.\n\n## Choose meaningful input and output\n\nIn general, it's recommended that operations have an input and/or output. If an observation has neither, ask yourself if an observation is actually useful or if you can drop it.\n\nThe **root observation** deserves the most care: the trace-level input and output are derived from it. They are shown in the tracing table, read by evaluators, and compared across runs in [dataset experiments](/docs/evaluation/experiments). Set them to what a reviewer needs at a glance — for a chatbot, the user message as input and the assistant response as output — not a raw JSON blob of function arguments. If you need the raw payload for debugging, put it in [metadata](/docs/observability/features/metadata).\n\nFor your **most viewed observations**, take some extra care to set them up. You will likely create pre-filtered views on your tracing and session screens. The observations you filter for here are the ones that will get looked at the most. For these, ask yourself: **what do I need to see to quickly evaluate a trace/session at a glance?**\n\n![Tracing table with input and output](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-tracing-table-io.png)\n\nTypical input/output for `GENERATION` observations:\n\n- For a chatbot: the user message (input) and the assistant response (output).\n- For a RAG pipeline: the user query and the generated answer.\n- For a classification task: the text being classified and the predicted label.\n\nMost inputs/outputs can be rendered as a readable, role-labeled conversation rather than a raw JSON blob. If yours show up as raw JSON, you can take a look at the formatting: it should be a list of messages in the standard OpenAI format (each with a `role` and `content`), and it renders tool calls as cards only when they sit in an assistant message's `tool_calls` array with each call's `arguments` given as a JSON-encoded string (for example `\"{\\\"location\\\": \\\"Paris\\\"}\"`).\n\nIf your input and output fields are showing up empty unintentionally, see [why are the input and output of my trace empty?](/faq/all/empty-trace-input-and-output)\n\n## Useful attributes\n\nObservations have a number of attributes that can be useful for your use cases. These will allow you to go even further with filtering, scoring, and making dashboards.\n\n### Add metadata for context\n\n[Metadata](/docs/observability/features/metadata) is a flexible key-value store on each observation. It's the right place for anything that is useful context but doesn't belong in the name or the input/output. Examples of metadata that is useful in practice:\n\n- **Evaluation context**: Ground truth, expected behavior, or other context an [LLM-as-a-judge evaluator](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) needs but that isn't part of the actual input/output. Evaluators can reference metadata fields in their variable mapping.\n- **Request context**: Internal request IDs, the API route or app version that handled the request, or the experiment variant / feature flags that were active. This lets you correlate a trace with your other systems and filter by rollout.\n- **Retrieval context**: For RAG steps, things like the data source, number of chunks retrieved, or the index queried — useful when debugging why a retrieval step returned poor results.\n- **Raw payloads**: Full request/response objects that would clutter the input/output fields but are occasionally needed for debugging.\n- **Annotation context**: When doing manual review, metadata gives annotators extra information to make better judgments.\n\nYou can filter by metadata keys in the Langfuse UI, which is helpful when you need to find traces with specific characteristics.\n\n### Track model, tokens, and cost on generations [#track-model-tokens-and-cost-on-generations]\n\nIf you want to understand what your LLM usage costs, broken down by model, by user, by feature, you need three things on your `generation` observations:\n\n- **Model name**: Langfuse uses this to look up pricing in the [model pricing table](/docs/model-usage-and-cost). If the model name doesn't match, Langfuse can't calculate cost automatically.\n- **Usage details**: Input tokens, output tokens, and optionally cached tokens. This is what powers the token usage views in dashboards.\n- **Cost details** (optional): If you want to override Langfuse's automatic pricing — for example, if you have a custom pricing agreement — you can pass cost explicitly.\n\nMost [integrations](/integrations) capture all of this automatically. If you're instrumenting manually, see the [token and cost tracking docs](/docs/observability/features/token-and-cost-tracking).\n\nYou can see these attributes on the `GENERATION` observation in the Langfuse UI.\n\n![Generation attributes in Langfuse](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-generation-attributes.png)\n\n### Use tags for business-level dimensions\n\n[Tags](/docs/observability/features/tags) enable filtering and metric breakdowns across dimensions that matter to your business. Good tags answer questions like \"how does latency differ between our `web` and `api` users?\".\n\nOne property of tags is that they are **immutable and must be set at observation creation time**. This makes them great for things you know upfront (where the request came from, which feature it's part of), but not for things you learn later.\n\nIf you need to label traces based on something determined after the fact, like an [LLM-as-a-judge](/docs/evaluation/evaluation-methods/llm-as-a-judge) evaluation result, use [scores](/docs/evaluation/overview) instead.\n\n### Link prompts to traces\n\nIf you [manage your prompts in Langfuse](/docs/prompt-management), you can [link them to your generations](/docs/prompt-management/features/link-to-traces). This lets you see which prompt version was used for a given trace, and track how metrics change across prompt versions. Useful when you're iterating on prompts and want to compare performance.\n\n### Set the environment\n\nSet the [environment](/docs/observability/features/environments) attribute (`production`, `staging`, `development`) so that your test traces don't pollute production dashboards and evaluations.\n\n### Track users with user IDs\n\nSetting the [user ID](/docs/observability/features/users) connects traces to specific users, which unlocks per-user views in Langfuse. Useful if you want to answer questions like:\n\n- Which users are costing us the most?\n- How does output quality vary across users?\n- What does a specific user's usage pattern look like?\n\n### Group related traces with session IDs\n\nIf your application involves multiple traces that logically belong together, group them into a [session](/docs/observability/features/sessions). This gives you a session replay view where you can see the full interaction in sequence.\n\nThis makes sense when:\n\n- You're building a chatbot (each user message creates a new trace, but the whole conversation is one session)\n- You have multiple agents that each contribute to a final output (e.g., five agents that collaborate to produce a report)\n- Your workflow spans multiple requests with human-in-the-loop steps in between\n\nIf your application is single-request/single-response with no continuity between calls, you probably don't need sessions.\n\n![Sessions view in Langfuse](/images/docs/faq/good-trace-sessions-view.png)\n\n<!-- agent-instructions -->\n\n---\n\n## Agent Instructions\n\nThis page is part of the [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com) documentation, published as plain Markdown for AI agents. Every page is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL, or by sending an `Accept: text/markdown` header. This page: `https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md`.\n\n### Querying these docs\n\nIf the answer is not on this page, query the documentation instead of guessing:\n\n- **Semantic search** across all Langfuse docs, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. Ask a specific, self-contained question:\n\n ```bash\n curl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n ```\n\n- **Index of every page**: <https://langfuse.com/llms.txt>, with per-section indexes [llms-docs.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-docs.txt), [llms-integrations.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-integrations.txt), and [llms-self-hosting.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-self-hosting.txt).\n\n### Before writing Langfuse code\n\n- **Install the [Langfuse Agent Skill](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill).** It encodes Langfuse's own best practices for instrumentation, prompt management, and evaluation, and materially improves results.\n- **Read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md)** before instrumenting an application.\n- **Verify endpoints, parameters, and response fields** against the [API reference](https://api.reference.langfuse.com) instead of inferring them from code examples.\n- **Use the [Langfuse CLI](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli)** (`npx langfuse-cli api <resource> <action>`) to read or write traces, prompts, datasets, and scores from the terminal.\n\nFound an error in these docs? Please open an issue at <https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/issues>.\n"}

{"type": "text", "text": "---\ntitle: Masking\ndescription: Configure masking to redact sensitive information from Langfuse SDK data and OpenTelemetry span attributes before they are sent to Langfuse.\nsidebarTitle: Masking\n---\n\n# Masking sensitive LLM data\n\nMasking gives you control over the [tracing](/docs/tracing/overview) data sent to Langfuse. Use masking functions to redact sensitive information before trace data leaves your application, for example to:\n\n1. Redact sensitive information from trace or observation inputs, outputs, and metadata.\n2. Transform OpenTelemetry span attributes before export.\n3. Implement fine-grained data filtering for compliance or privacy requirements.\n\nLearn more about Langfuse's data security and privacy measures concerning the stored data in our [security and compliance overview](/security).\n\n## Configure masking\n\n<LangTabs items={[\"Python SDK\", \"JS/TS SDK\", \"LangChain (JS/TS)\"]}>\n<Tab title=\"Python SDK\">\n\nThe Python SDK supports two masking hooks. For new Python SDK setups, prefer `mask_otel_spans`.\n\n| Method | Status | When it runs | What it covers |\n| ----------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| `mask_otel_spans` | Recommended | At export stage, after Langfuse decides which OpenTelemetry spans this client should export and after Langfuse media handling | Raw OpenTelemetry span attributes from Langfuse SDK spans and third-party instrumentations exported by this Langfuse client |\n| `mask` | Legacy | Synchronously when Langfuse SDK attributes are created | Data set through Langfuse SDK APIs such as `start_observation()`, `update()`, and `set_trace_io()` |\n\nUse `mask_otel_spans` to patch OpenTelemetry span attributes before the Langfuse client exports them. The hook receives read-only snapshots of one OpenTelemetry export batch and returns sparse patches for the spans that should change.\n\n```python\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\nfrom langfuse.types import (\n MaskOtelSpansParams,\n MaskOtelSpansResult,\n OtelSpanPatch,\n)\n\n\ndef mask_otel_spans(\n *, params: MaskOtelSpansParams\n) -> Optional[MaskOtelSpansResult]:\n patches = {}\n\n for identifier, span in params.spans.items():\n if span.instrumentation_scope_name == \"openai\":\n patches[identifier] = OtelSpanPatch(\n delete_attributes=(\n \"gen_ai.prompt.0.content\",\n \"gen_ai.completion.0.content\",\n ),\n set_attributes={\"masking.applied\": True},\n )\n\n return MaskOtelSpansResult(span_patches=patches)\n\n\nlangfuse = Langfuse(mask_otel_spans=mask_otel_spans)\n```\n\n### `mask_otel_spans` behavior\n\n`mask_otel_spans` follows the public Python SDK type contract:\n\n- It receives one OpenTelemetry export batch as `params.spans`. A batch is not guaranteed to contain a complete trace, request, or Langfuse observation tree.\n- Each key is an `OtelSpanIdentifier(trace_id, span_id)`. Reuse the identifier objects from `params.spans` when returning patches.\n- Each value is an `OtelSpanData` snapshot after `should_export_span` filtering and export-stage media handling. Its `attributes` and `resource_attributes` mappings are read-only.\n- Return `None` to leave the whole batch unchanged.\n- Return `MaskOtelSpansResult(span_patches=...)` to delete or replace attributes on selected spans.\n- Patches are sparse. Omit spans that do not need changes.\n- `OtelSpanPatch` deletes `delete_attributes` first and then applies `set_attributes`, so `set_attributes` wins when the same key appears in both.\n- `set_attributes` values must be valid OpenTelemetry attribute values: strings, booleans, integers, floats, or homogeneous sequences of those scalar types.\n- The hook can only change span attributes. It cannot change the span name, IDs, parent relationship, resource attributes, events, links, or instrumentation scope.\n- The hook affects only spans exported by this Langfuse client. If the same OpenTelemetry spans are sent to another exporter, that exporter receives its own unmodified copy.\n\n`mask_otel_spans` only affects spans that pass through the Langfuse Python SDK span processor and are exported by this Langfuse client. If you also send telemetry to another observability backend through a separate OpenTelemetry span processor or exporter, that backend receives its own unmodified copy of the spans. Configure masking separately for any non-Langfuse exporter.\n\n`mask_otel_spans` is synchronous. It usually runs on the OpenTelemetry batch span processor worker thread, so it should not block the main caller thread of your application. During `flush()` and shutdown it may run on the caller thread.\n\nKeep the function deterministic and fast. Network calls are possible, but slow masking backs up the OpenTelemetry export queue and delays span export. Avoid long-running work, unbounded retries, request-local state, the current active span, and async I/O inside the masking function.\n\nIf `mask_otel_spans` raises an exception or returns an invalid `MaskOtelSpansResult`, Langfuse drops the whole export batch. If an individual `OtelSpanPatch` is invalid, Langfuse drops only that span from the Langfuse export. Invalid returned attribute values delete only the affected attribute.\n\n### Legacy `mask` behavior\n\nThe `mask` parameter is the legacy Python SDK masking hook. It runs synchronously when Langfuse SDK attributes are created and applies only to data set through Langfuse SDK APIs such as `start_observation()`, `update()`, and `set_trace_io()`. It does not inspect final raw OpenTelemetry span attributes from third-party instrumentations.\n\nUse `mask` only when you specifically need to transform data at Langfuse SDK attribute creation time.\n\n```python\nfrom typing import Any\n\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\n\n\ndef masking_function(*, data: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Any:\n if isinstance(data, str) and data.startswith(\"SECRET_\"):\n return \"REDACTED\"\n\n if isinstance(data, dict):\n return {key: masking_function(data=value) for key, value in data.items()}\n\n if isinstance(data, list):\n return [masking_function(data=item) for item in data]\n\n return data\n\n\nlangfuse = Langfuse(mask=masking_function)\n```\n\nFor new Python SDK masking setups, prefer `mask_otel_spans`.\n\n### Examples\n\n#### Redact credit card numbers with `mask_otel_spans`\n\nThis example scans exported OpenTelemetry string attributes for credit card-like patterns and replaces matches before the span is exported to Langfuse.\n\n```python\nimport re\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse, observe\nfrom langfuse.types import (\n MaskOtelSpansParams,\n MaskOtelSpansResult,\n OtelSpanPatch,\n)\n\ncredit_card_pattern = re.compile(r\"\\b(?:\\d[ -]*?){13,19}\\b\")\n\n\ndef mask_otel_spans(\n *, params: MaskOtelSpansParams\n) -> Optional[MaskOtelSpansResult]:\n patches = {}\n\n for identifier, span in params.spans.items():\n replacements = {}\n\n for key, value in span.attributes.items():\n if isinstance(value, str):\n masked_value = credit_card_pattern.sub(\n \"[REDACTED CREDIT CARD]\", value\n )\n\n if masked_value != value:\n replacements[key] = masked_value\n\n if replacements:\n patches[identifier] = OtelSpanPatch(set_attributes=replacements)\n\n return MaskOtelSpansResult(span_patches=patches)\n\n\nlangfuse = Langfuse(mask_otel_spans=mask_otel_spans)\n\n\n@observe()\ndef process_payment():\n return \"Customer paid with card number 4111 1111 1111 1111.\"\n\n\nresult = process_payment()\n\nprint(result)\n# Output: Customer paid with card number 4111 1111 1111 1111.\n\n# Flush spans in short-lived applications.\nlangfuse.flush()\n```\n\nThe function result printed in your application is unchanged. The exported span attributes sent to Langfuse contain the redacted value.\n\n#### Redact email addresses and phone numbers\n\n```python\nimport re\nfrom typing import Optional\n\nfrom langfuse import Langfuse\nfrom langfuse.types import (\n MaskOtelSpansParams,\n MaskOtelSpansResult,\n OtelSpanPatch,\n)\n\nemail_pattern = re.compile(r\"\\b[\\w.-]+?@[\\w.-]+?\\.\\w+?\\b\")\nphone_pattern = re.compile(r\"\\b\\d{3}[-. ]?\\d{3}[-. ]?\\d{4}\\b\")\n\n\ndef mask_otel_spans(\n *, params: MaskOtelSpansParams\n) -> Optional[MaskOtelSpansResult]:\n patches = {}\n\n for identifier, span in params.spans.items():\n replacements = {}\n\n for key, value in span.attributes.items():\n if isinstance(value, str):\n masked_value = email_pattern.sub(\"[REDACTED EMAIL]\", value)\n masked_value = phone_pattern.sub(\"[REDACTED PHONE]\", masked_value)\n\n if masked_value != value:\n replacements[key] = masked_value\n\n if replacements:\n patches[identifier] = OtelSpanPatch(set_attributes=replacements)\n\n return MaskOtelSpansResult(span_patches=patches)\n\n\nlangfuse = Langfuse(mask_otel_spans=mask_otel_spans)\n```\n\n</Tab>\n<Tab title=\"JS/TS SDK\">\n\nTo prevent sensitive data from being sent to Langfuse, you can provide a `mask` function to the `LangfuseSpanProcessor`. This function will be applied to the `input`, `output`, and `metadata` of every observation.\n\nThe function receives an object `{ data }`, where `data` is the stringified JSON of the attribute's value. It should return the masked data.\n\n```ts filename=\"instrumentation.ts\" /mask:/\nimport { NodeSDK } from \"@opentelemetry/sdk-node\";\nimport { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from \"@langfuse/otel\";\n\nconst spanProcessor = new LangfuseSpanProcessor({\n mask: ({ data }) => {\n const maskedData = data.replace(\n /\\b\\d{4}[- ]?\\d{4}[- ]?\\d{4}[- ]?\\d{4}\\b/g,\n \"***MASKED_CREDIT_CARD***\",\n );\n\n return maskedData;\n },\n});\n\nconst sdk = new NodeSDK({\n spanProcessors: [spanProcessor],\n});\n\nsdk.start();\n```\n\nSee [JS/TS SDK docs](/docs/sdk/typescript/guide) for more details.\n\n</Tab>\n<Tab title=\"LangChain (JS/TS)\">\n\nMasking is configured on the `LangfuseSpanProcessor` — spans created by the LangChain [CallbackHandler](/integrations/frameworks/langchain) flow through it automatically, so no LangChain-specific masking setup is needed:\n\n```typescript\nimport { NodeSDK } from \"@opentelemetry/sdk-node\";\nimport { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from \"@langfuse/otel\";\nimport { CallbackHandler } from \"@langfuse/langchain\";\n\nconst spanProcessor = new LangfuseSpanProcessor({\n mask: ({ data }) => {\n if (typeof data === \"string\" && data.startsWith(\"SECRET_\")) {\n return \"REDACTED\";\n }\n\n return data;\n },\n});\n\nconst sdk = new NodeSDK({ spanProcessors: [spanProcessor] });\nsdk.start();\n\nconst handler = new CallbackHandler();\n```\n\n</Tab>\n</LangTabs>\n\n## Masking with OpenTelemetry\n\nIn a pure OpenTelemetry tracing setup, mask sensitive span attributes before they reach Langfuse. You can apply masking in two places:\n\n- **In the application:** Avoid recording sensitive attributes where possible. Otherwise, use a language-specific or custom span processor or export layer to transform them before OTLP export. Choose this approach when sensitive data must not leave the application.\n- **In an OpenTelemetry Collector:** Route traces through an optional Collector and use the attributes, redaction, or transform processors to mask attributes centrally. The filter processor drops entire spans, so use it only when you intentionally want to remove spans. This approach is useful for applying a consistent policy across multiple services.\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n App[\"Application (OpenTelemetry SDK)\"] -->|\"OTLP traces\"| Collector[\"OpenTelemetry Collector<br/>(masking processors)\"]\n Collector -->|\"OTLP/HTTP\"| Langfuse[\"Langfuse\"]\n```\n\nCollector-side masking happens after telemetry leaves the application. Deploy the Collector within the appropriate trust boundary and secure the connection between the application and Collector.\n\nSee OpenTelemetry's guide to [handling sensitive data](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/security/handling-sensitive-data/) for common Collector processor patterns, and the [Langfuse OpenTelemetry integration guide](/integrations/native/opentelemetry) for export setup.\n\n## Related resources\n\n- [Data Retention](/docs/administration/data-retention) - Automatically delete traces, observations, scores, and media assets after a configured retention period.\n- [Data Deletion](/docs/administration/data-deletion) - Manually delete individual or batches of traces.\n\n## GitHub discussions\n\n<!-- agent-instructions -->\n\n---\n\n## Agent Instructions\n\nThis page is part of the [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com) documentation, published as plain Markdown for AI agents. Every page is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL, or by sending an `Accept: text/markdown` header. This page: `https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/masking.md`.\n\n### Querying these docs\n\nIf the answer is not on this page, query the documentation instead of guessing:\n\n- **Semantic search** across all Langfuse docs, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. Ask a specific, self-contained question:\n\n ```bash\n curl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n ```\n\n- **Index of every page**: <https://langfuse.com/llms.txt>, with per-section indexes [llms-docs.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-docs.txt), [llms-integrations.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-integrations.txt), and [llms-self-hosting.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-self-hosting.txt).\n\n### Before writing Langfuse code\n\n- **Install the [Langfuse Agent Skill](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill).** It encodes Langfuse's own best practices for instrumentation, prompt management, and evaluation, and materially improves results.\n- **Read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md)** before instrumenting an application.\n- **Verify endpoints, parameters, and response fields** against the [API reference](https://api.reference.langfuse.com) instead of inferring them from code examples.\n- **Use the [Langfuse CLI](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli)** (`npx langfuse-cli api <resource> <action>`) to read or write traces, prompts, datasets, and scores from the terminal.\n\nFound an error in these docs? Please open an issue at <https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/issues>.\n"}

{"type": "text", "text": "---\ntitle: Access Control (RBAC)\ndescription: Langfuse offers extensive RBAC capabilities to manage project sharing and permissions across different organizations and projects.\nsidebarTitle: Access Control (RBAC)\n---\n\n# Role-Based Access Controls in Langfuse\n\nThe role-based access control (RBAC) in Langfuse is based on users, organizations, projects, and roles:\n\n- `Users` are [authenticated](/docs/administration/authentication-and-sso) individuals who access Langfuse\n- `Organizations` are the top-level entities that contain projects.\n- `Projects` group all Langfuse data to allow for fine-grained role-based access control (RBAC).\n- `Roles` define the permissions of users within an organization and project:\n - By default, users get assigned a role on the organizational level.\n - For more fine-grained control, users can be assigned project-roles. This is useful when you want to differentiate permissions for different projects within the same organization.\n\n`API Keys` are used to authenticate with the Langfuse API. They are associated with a project and can be used to access the project's data programmatically. API keys are not tied to a user.\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n A[\"User (via UI)\"] -->|role| B[Organization]\n B -->|1:n| C[Projects]\n A -.->|optional: project-role| C\n D[API Keys] -->|n:1| C\n```\n\n## Access Organizations and Projects\n\nYou can easily switch between organizations and projects using the dropdowns in the top navigation bar.\n\n## Roles and Scopes\n\n- `Owner`: has all permissions\n- `Admin`: can edit the project settings and grant access to other users\n- `Member`: can view all metrics & create scores, but cannot configure the project\n- `Viewer`: view-only access to the project and organization, most of the configuration is hidden\n- `None`: no default access to the organization, to be used when user should have access to a single project only\n\nexport function RolePermissionTable({ roleScopes }) {\n return (\n \n {Object.entries(roleScopes).map(([role, scopes]) => (\n \n {role}\n {scopes\n .sort((a, b) => a.localeCompare(b))\n .map((scope) => (\n \n {scope}\n \n ))}\n \n ))}\n \n );\n}\n\n<Accordion type=\"single\" collapsible>\n <AccordionItem value=\"organization-scopes\">\n <AccordionTrigger>Organization-level scopes</AccordionTrigger>\n \n </AccordionItem>\n <AccordionItem value=\"project-scopes\">\n <AccordionTrigger>Project-level scopes</AccordionTrigger>\n \n </AccordionItem>\n</Accordion>\n\n## Managing users\n\n### Add a new user to an organization\n\nIn the organization settings, you can add users via their email address and assign them a role. They will receive an email notification and will be able to access the organization once they log in. Users who do not have a Langfuse account yet, will be listed as pending invites until they sign up.\n\n### Changing user roles\n\nAny user with the `members:CUD` permission can change the role of a user in the organization settings. This will affect the user's permissions across all projects in the organization. Users can only assign roles that are lower or equal to their own role.\n\n## Managing Projects\n\n### Add a new project\n\nAny user with the `projects:create` permission can create a new project within a Langfuse organization.\n\n### Transfer a project to another organization\n\nOnly users with the `projects:transfer_organization` permission can transfer a project to another organization. This will remove the project from the current organization and add it to the new one. Access to the project will depend on the roles configured in the new organization.\n\nDuring this process, no data will be lost, all project settings, data, and configurations will be transferred to the new organization. The project remains fully operational as API keys, settings (except for access management), and data will remain unchanged and associated with the project. All features (e.g. tracing, prompt management) will continue to work without any interruption.\n\n## Project-level roles\n\n**Where is this feature available?**\n\n| Plan | Availability |\n| --- | --- |\n| Hobby | Not Available |\n| Core | Not Available |\n| Pro | Teams Add-on required |\n| Enterprise | Available |\n| Self Hosted | Enterprise Edition |\n\nUsers by default inherit the role of the organization they are part of. For more fine-grained control, you can assign a user a role on the project level. This is useful when you want to differentiate permissions for different projects within the same organization.\n\nIf a project-level role is assigned, it will override the organization-level role for that project.\n\nIf you want to give a user access to only certain projects within an organization, you can set their role to `None` on the organization level and then assign them a role on the project level.\n\n## Related Resources\n\n- [SCIM & Organization API](/docs/administration/scim-and-org-api) to programmatically manage users, roles, projects, and API keys\n- [How to structure projects and environments](/faq/all/managing-different-environments) for production, staging, and development\n\n## GitHub Discussions\n\n<!-- agent-instructions -->\n\n---\n\n## Agent Instructions\n\nThis page is part of the [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com) documentation, published as plain Markdown for AI agents. Every page is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL, or by sending an `Accept: text/markdown` header. This page: `https://langfuse.com/docs/administration/rbac.md`.\n\n### Querying these docs\n\nIf the answer is not on this page, query the documentation instead of guessing:\n\n- **Semantic search** across all Langfuse docs, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. Ask a specific, self-contained question:\n\n ```bash\n curl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n ```\n\n- **Index of every page**: <https://langfuse.com/llms.txt>, with per-section indexes [llms-docs.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-docs.txt), [llms-integrations.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-integrations.txt), and [llms-self-hosting.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-self-hosting.txt).\n\n### Before writing Langfuse code\n\n- **Install the [Langfuse Agent Skill](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill).** It encodes Langfuse's own best practices for instrumentation, prompt management, and evaluation, and materially improves results.\n- **Read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md)** before instrumenting an application.\n- **Verify endpoints, parameters, and response fields** against the [API reference](https://api.reference.langfuse.com) instead of inferring them from code examples.\n- **Use the [Langfuse CLI](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli)** (`npx langfuse-cli api <resource> <action>`) to read or write traces, prompts, datasets, and scores from the terminal.\n\nFound an error in these docs? Please open an issue at <https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/issues>.\n"}

{"type": "text", "text": "---\ntitle: OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability\ndescription: Connect Langfuse to OpenTelemetry (OTEL) and send OTLP traces from your application or collector to Langfuse.\nshortTitle: Overview\nsidebarTitle: OpenTelemetry\nlogo: /images/integrations/opentelemetry_icon.svg\n---\n\n# OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability\n\n[OpenTelemetry (OTEL)](https://opentelemetry.io/) is a [CNCF](https://www.cncf.io/) project that provides a set of specifications, APIs, and libraries that define a standard way to collect distributed traces and metrics from your application.\n\nUse this page if your application, framework, or collector already emits OpenTelemetry (OTEL) traces and you want to send them to Langfuse.\n\n **Using Python or JavaScript/TypeScript?** Use the [Langfuse SDK](/docs/observability/sdk/overview) instead of building directly on the OTEL API. The SDK handles Langfuse attributes, propagation, media, filtering, and export for you. For other languages, use the [native OpenTelemetry API for your language](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/) and export spans to Langfuse.\n\n## OpenTelemetry endpoint [#opentelemetry-endpoint]\n\nLangfuse can receive traces on the `/api/public/otel` (OTLP) endpoint.\n\nIf you use a Collector that uses the OpenTelemetry SDK to export traces, you can use the following configuration:\n\n```bash\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\" # 🇪🇺 EU data region\n# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\n# OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=\"http://localhost:3000/api/public/otel\" # 🏠 Local deployment (>= v3.22.0)\n\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=\"Authorization=Basic ${AUTH_STRING},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4\"\n```\n\nLangfuse uses [Basic Auth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication) to authenticate requests.\n\nYou can use the following command to get the base64 encoded API keys (referred to as `AUTH_STRING`): `echo -n \"pk-lf-1234567890:sk-lf-1234567890\" | base64`.\nFor long API Keys on GNU systems, you may have to add `-w 0` at the end since `base64` auto-wraps columns.\n\n### Enable real-time ingestion in Langfuse v4 [#real-time-ingestion]\n\nIf you send spans directly via OpenTelemetry, include the\n`x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4` header so that new data appears in real time\non the v4 data model and the v2 Observations and Metrics APIs. Without\nthis header, directly ingested OpenTelemetry data can be delayed by up to 10\nminutes. The `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` configuration above already includes\nthe header.\n\nIf your setup uses signal-specific header settings, configure the same header\non the traces exporter:\n\n```bash\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_HEADERS=\"Authorization=Basic ${AUTH_STRING},x-langfuse-ingestion-version=4\"\n```\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\n\nIf your collector requires signal-specific environment variables, the trace endpoint is `/api/public/otel/v1/traces`.\n\n```bash\nOTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=\"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces\" # EU data region\n# Other Langfuse data regions include 🇺🇸 US: https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces, 🇯🇵 Japan: https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces and ⚕️ HIPAA: https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel/v1/traces\n```\n\n</Callout>\n\nPlease note that Langfuse currently supports OTLP over HTTP with both `HTTP/JSON` and `HTTP/protobuf`. `gRPC` is not supported yet.\n\n **Migrating to Langfuse v4?** If you send custom events to the legacy `/api/public/ingestion` endpoint, or already send OTEL spans that rely on trace input/output or root-only attributes, follow the [custom ingestion migration guide](/integrations/native/opentelemetry/migration-to-v4).\n\nLangfuse can operate as an OpenTelemetry Backend to receive traces on the `/api/public/otel` (OTLP) endpoint. In addition to the [Langfuse SDKs](/docs/sdk/overview) and [native integrations](/integrations), this OpenTelemetry endpoint is designed to increase compatibility with frameworks, libraries, and languages beyond the SDKs and native integrations. Popular OpenTelemetry libraries include OpenLLMetry and OpenLIT which extend Language support of Langfuse tracing to Java and Go and cover frameworks such as AutoGen, Semantic Kernel, and more.\n\nAs the [Semantic Conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/attributes-registry/gen-ai/) for GenAI attributes on traces are still evolving, Langfuse maps the received OTel traces to the [Langfuse data model](/docs/observability/data-model) and supports additional attributes that are popular in the OTel GenAI ecosystem ([attribute mapping](#property-mapping)). Please contribute to the discussion on [GitHub](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/2509) if an integration does not work as expected or does not parse the correct attributes.\n\n> **Using other OTEL-based tools?** If you're using Langfuse alongside other OpenTelemetry-based tools, you may run into conflicts. See [Using Langfuse with an Existing OpenTelemetry Setup](/faq/all/existing-otel-setup) for configuration guidance.\n\n **Important:** If you want to filter and aggregate by `userId`, `sessionId`,\n `metadata`, `version`, `release`, or `tags`, you need to propagate these\n trace-level attributes to every span in the trace. Start with\n [Propagating Trace Attributes to All Spans](#propagating-attributes) before\n wiring this up in production.\n\n OTLP replaces the deprecated `POST /api/public/ingestion` API. See\n [Migration of deprecated APIs](/faq/all/deprecated-api-migration#ingestion) for\n the endpoint mapping; the deprecated endpoint itself is documented in its\n [endpoint reference section](/faq/all/deprecated-api-migration#endpoints).\n\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n subgraph App[\"Application\"]\n Logic[\"Operations, LLM calls, events\"]\n OTel[\"OpenTelemetry instrumentation (SDKs, libraries)\"]\n Logic --> OTel\n end\n\n OTel -->|\"OTLP traces\"| Endpoint[\"Langfuse OTLP endpoint /api/public/otel\"]\n\n subgraph Langfuse[\"Langfuse\"]\n Endpoint --> Map[\"OTel to Langfuse attribute mapping\"]\n Map --> UI[\"Langfuse data model\"]\n end\n\n classDef subgraphBox fill:none,stroke:#888,stroke-width:2px;\n class App,Langfuse subgraphBox;\n```\n\n## Important: Propagating Trace Attributes to All Spans [#propagating-attributes]\n\nWhen using OpenTelemetry (OTEL) instrumentation to send traces to Langfuse,\ncertain trace-level attributes should be propagated to **all spans** within a\ntrace to enable accurate aggregations and filtering in Langfuse. These\nattributes include:\n\n- `userId` (via `langfuse.user.id` or `user.id`)\n- `sessionId` (via `langfuse.session.id` or `session.id`)\n- `metadata` (via `langfuse.trace.metadata.*` for top-level metadata keys)\n- `version` (via `langfuse.version`)\n- `release` (via `langfuse.release`)\n- `tags` (via `langfuse.trace.tags`)\n- `trace_name` (via `langfuse.trace.name`)\n\nLangfuse filters and aggregations increasingly operate across individual\nobservations rather than only at the trace level. If you want to reliably\nfilter or aggregate by these attributes, they need to be present on each span\nin the trace, not only on the root span.\n\n### Recommended: Use OpenTelemetry Baggage for Propagation [#recommended-use-opentelemetry-baggage-for-propagation]\n\nThe recommended approach for propagating these attributes across all spans is\nto use [OpenTelemetry Baggage](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/baggage/)\nwith a `BaggageSpanProcessor`. Baggage is a built-in OpenTelemetry mechanism\nfor context propagation that automatically copies specified key-value pairs to\nall spans within a trace context.\n\nTo implement this pattern:\n\n1. Set the desired attributes as baggage entries at the beginning of your trace.\n2. Set the attributes on the currently active span.\n3. Configure a `BaggageSpanProcessor` in your OpenTelemetry setup to automatically copy baggage entries to span attributes.\n4. The processor will ensure all downstream spans in the trace context receive these attributes.\n\nFor implementation details and code examples, refer to the OpenTelemetry\ndocumentation for\n[Python](https://pypi.org/project/opentelemetry-processor-baggage/) and\n[JavaScript](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opentelemetry/baggage-span-processor).\n\n **Security Consideration:** OpenTelemetry baggage is propagated across\n service boundaries and to third-party APIs. **Do not include sensitive\n information** (passwords, API keys, personal data, etc.) in baggage when\n using this approach, as it will be transmitted to all downstream services.\n\n### Alternative: Use Langfuse SDK Helpers\n\nIf you're using the [Langfuse SDKs](/docs/observability/sdk/overview) with\nOpenTelemetry integration, you can use the convenience methods\n`propagate_attributes()` (Python) or `propagateAttributes()` (TypeScript),\nwhich handle attribute propagation automatically. These methods provide a\nsimpler interface and are the recommended approach when using Langfuse SDKs.\n\n## Ingestion Options\n\n### OpenTelemetry native Langfuse SDK v4\n\nThe quickest path to start tracing with Langfuse is the new **OTEL-native Langfuse SDK v4**. The SDK is a thin layer on top of the official OpenTelemetry client that automatically converts emitted spans into rich Langfuse observations (spans, generations, events, and [other observation types](/docs/observability/features/observation-types)) and adds first-class helpers for LLM-specific features such as token usage, cost tracking, prompt linking, and scoring.\n\nBecause it lives in the shared OpenTelemetry context, spans from other OTEL-instrumented libraries can be exported to Langfuse too. By default, Langfuse focuses on LLM-relevant spans (Langfuse SDK spans, spans with `gen_ai.*` attributes, and known LLM instrumentors). To export everything, use a permissive custom filter as described in the [advanced SDK docs](/docs/observability/sdk/advanced-features#filtering-by-instrumentation-scope).\n\nGet started by following the dedicated guide for the Python implementation here: [/docs/observability/sdk/overview](/docs/observability/sdk/overview).\n\n### Custom via OpenTelemetry SDKs\n\nYou can use the OpenTelemetry SDKs to directly export traces to Langfuse with the configuration mentioned above. Thereby, Language support of Langfuse is extended to other languages than the ones supported by the [Langfuse SDKs](/docs/sdk/overview) (Python and JS/TS).\n\n### Run experiments via OpenTelemetry [#experiments-ingesting-experiment-spans]\n\nTo group direct-OTEL traces as Langfuse experiments, start with [Experiments via OpenTelemetry](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-opentelemetry) and then add the experiment and item attributes described in [Ingest experiment spans with OpenTelemetry](/integrations/native/opentelemetry/experiments).\n\n### Use OpenTelemetry GenAI Instrumentation Libraries\n\nAny OpenTelemetry compatible instrumentation can be used to export traces to Langfuse. Check out the following end-to-end examples of popular instrumentation SDKs to get started:\n\n**Libraries**\n\n- [OpenLIT](/docs/opentelemetry/example-openlit)\n- [OpenLLMetry](/docs/opentelemetry/example-openllmetry)\n- [Arize](/docs/opentelemetry/example-arize)\n- [MLflow](/docs/opentelemetry/example-mlflow)\n\n<Details>\n\n<Summary>Comparison of OpenTelemetry Instrumentation Libraries</Summary>\n\n| Category | Item | OpenLLMetry | openlit | Arize |\n| ---------- | ----------------------------- | ----------- | ------- | ----- |\n| LLMs | AI21 | | ✅ | |\n| | Aleph Alpha | ✅ | | |\n| | Amazon Bedrock | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\n| | Anthropic | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |\n| | Assembly AI | use a permissive custom filter as described in the [advanced SDK docs](/docs/observability/sdk/advanced-features#filtering-by-instrumentation-scope).\n\nGet started by following the dedicated guide for the Python implementation here: [/docs/observability/sdk/overview](/docs/observability/sdk/overview).\n\n### Custom via OpenTelemetry SDKs\n\nYou can use the OpenTelemetry SDKs to directly export traces to Langfuse with the configuration mentioned above. Thereby, Language support of Langfuse is extended to other languages than the ones supported by the [Langfuse SDKs](/docs/sdk/overview) (Python and JS/TS).\n\n### Run experiments via OpenTelemetry [#experiments-ingesting-experiment-spans]\n\nTo group direct-OTEL traces as Langfuse experiments, start with [Experiments via OpenTelemetry](/docs/evaluation/experiments/experiments-via-opentelemetry) and then add the experiment and item attributes described in [Ingest experiment spans with OpenTelemetry](/integrations/native/opentelemetry/experiments).\n\n### Use OpenTelemetry GenAI Instrumentation Libraries\n\nAny OpenTelemetry compatible instrumentation can be used to export traces to Langfuse. Check out the following end-to-end examples of popular instrumentation SDKs to get started:\n\n**Libraries**\n\n- [OpenLIT](/docs/opentelemetry/example-openlit)\n- AI](/integrations/frameworks/spring-ai)\n- [LlamaIndex](/integrations/frameworks/llamaindex)\n- [LlamaIndex Workflows](/integrations/frameworks/llamaindex-workflows)\n\n### Export from OpenTelemetry Collector\n\n```mermaid\ngraph LR\n A[Application with OTel Instrumentation] --> B[OpenTelemetry Collector]\n B --> C[Langfuse]\n```\n\nIf you run an [OpenTelemetry Collector](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/collector), you can use the following configuration to export traces to Langfuse:\n\n```yml\nreceivers:\n otlp:\n protocols:\n grpc:\n endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317\n http:\n endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318\n\nprocessors:\n batch:\n memory_limiter:\n # 80% of maximum memory up to 2G\n limit_mib: 1500\n # 25% of limit up to 2G\n spike_limit_mib: 512\n check_interval: 5s\n\nexporters:\n otlphttp/langfuse:\n endpoint: \"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\" # EU data region\n # Other regions: US https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel, Japan https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel, HIPAA https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\n headers:\n Authorization: \"Basic ${AUTH_STRING}\" # Previously encoded API keys\n x-langfuse-ingestion-version: \"4\"\n\nservice:\n pipelines:\n traces:\n receivers: [otlp]\n processors: [memory_limiter, batch]\n exporters: [otlphttp/langfuse]\n```\n\n#### Filtering Spans sent to Langfuse\n\nIn case you want to selectively send OTel Spans to Langfuse, you can use the OTel Collector [filterprocessor](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/blob/main/processor/filterprocessor/README.md).\nIt enables you to filter spans based on attributes, span names, and more.\nAs this applies on a Span level, you may risk incomplete traces and should be careful when applying complex filter rules.\nLangfuse also requires that a root span is sent to our backend to ensure that a trace is created correctly.\n\nWith the configuration below, you would only forward Spans which have a `gen_ai.system` attribute set to `openai`:\n\n```yml\nreceivers:\n otlp:\n protocols:\n grpc:\n endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317\n http:\n endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318\n\nprocessors:\n filter/openaisystem:\n error_mode: ignore\n traces:\n span:\n - 'attributes[\"gen_ai.system\"] != \"openai\"'\n\nexporters:\n otlphttp/langfuse:\n endpoint: \"https://cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\" # EU data region\n # Other regions: US https://us.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel, Japan https://jp.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel, HIPAA https://hipaa.cloud.langfuse.com/api/public/otel\n headers:\n Authorization: \"Basic ${AUTH_STRING}\" # Previously encoded API keys\n x-langfuse-ingestion-version: \"4\"\n\nservice:\n pipelines:\n traces:\n receivers: [otlp]\n processors: [filter/openaisystem]\n exporters: [otlphttp/langfuse]\n```\n\n## Attribute Mapping [#property-mapping]\n\nLangfuse aims to be compliant with the [OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans/) and support major LLM instrumentation frameworks.\n\nFurthermore, Langfuse uses attributes within the `langfuse.*` namespace to map OpenTelemetry span attributes directly to the Langfuse data model. These specific attributes always take precedence over the generic OpenTelemetry conventions and are recommended for all users that are manually instrumenting their applications.\n\n Please [raise an issue on GitHub](/issues) if any mapping or integration does\n not work as expected or does not parse the correct attributes.\n\n **Reserved attribute key segments:** Attribute keys that contain `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` as a path segment (e.g. `gen_ai.prompt.__proto__.foo`) are silently dropped during ingestion. This is a security measure to prevent prototype pollution. If you notice missing attributes, check that your keys do not include these reserved segments.\n\nLangfuse distinguishes between trace-level attributes and observation-level attributes.\n\n- [Trace-level attributes](#trace-level-attributes) represent shared context for an entire interaction. If Langfuse detects these attributes on a specific span, it will treat them as properties of the whole trace.\n- [Observation-level attributes](#observation-level-attributes) describe individual steps within a trace. Langfuse keeps them on the observation level.\n\n### How Metadata Mapping Works [#metadata-mapping]\n\nOpenTelemetry spans can carry arbitrary attributes. Langfuse handles these attributes differently depending on how they are named:\n\n| Attribute Type | Where it Appears in Langfuse | Example |\n| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| **Explicit metadata mapping** | First-level key in `metadata` (filterable) | `langfuse.trace.metadata.customer_tier` → `metadata.customer_tier` |\n| **Unmapped OTel attributes** | Nested under `metadata.attributes` (catch-all) | `http.method` → `metadata.attributes.http.method` |\n| **Resource attributes** | Nested under `metadata.resourceAttributes` | `service.name` → `metadata.resourceAttributes.service.name` |\n\n**Langfuse SDKs vs. standard OpenTelemetry SDKs**\n\n- **Langfuse SDKs** provide utility functions (like `update()` with a `metadata` parameter) that automatically set the `langfuse.*.metadata.*` prefixed attributes. This means custom metadata appears at the first level and is filterable.\n- **Standard OpenTelemetry SDKs** set attributes directly on spans. Unless you explicitly use the `langfuse.trace.metadata.*` or `langfuse.observation.metadata.*` prefix, these attributes end up in the `metadata.attributes` catch-all and are not directly filterable in Langfuse.\n\n### Trace-Level Attributes\n\nThese attributes are applied to the trace record in Langfuse. They may be set on any span in the trace.\n\n| Langfuse Field | Description | Mapped from OTel Attribute |\n| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n| <a id=\"name\"></a>`name` | The name of the trace. | • `langfuse.trace.name`: `string`<br/>• Span name of the root span |\n| <a id=\"userId\"></a>`userId` | The unique identifier for the end-user. | • `langfuse.user.id`: `string`<br/>• `user.id`: `string` |\n| <a id=\"sessionId\"></a>`sessionId` | The unique identifier for the user session. | • `langfuse.session.id`: `string`<br/>• `session.id`: `string` |\n| <a id=\"release\"></a>`release` | The release version of your application. | • `langfuse.release`: `string` |\n| <a id=\"public\"></a>`public` | A boolean flag to mark a trace as public, allowing it to be shared via a URL. | • `langfuse.trace.public`: `boolean` |\n| <a id=\"tags\"></a>`tags` | An array of strings to categorize or label the trace. | • `langfuse.trace.tags`: `string[]` |\n| <a id=\"metadata\"></a>`metadata` | A flexible object for storing any additional, unstructured data on the trace. See note below. | • `langfuse.trace.metadata.*`: `string`<br/>• Root span's observation metadata |\n| <a id=\"input\"></a>`input` | Deprecated trace input, retained for legacy trace-level evaluators. In v4, use the root observation's input. | • `langfuse.trace.input`: `string`<br/>• Root span's observation input |\n| <a id=\"output\"></a>`output` | Deprecated trace output, retained for legacy trace-level evaluators. In v4, use the root observation's output. | • `langfuse.trace.output`: `string`<br/>• Root span's observation output |\n| <a id=\"version\"></a>`version` | The [version](/docs/observability/features/releases-and-versioning) of the trace, useful for tracking changes to your application logic. | • Root span's attributes mapped to `version` |\n| <a id=\"environment\"></a>`environment` | The deployment [environment](/docs/observability/features/environments) where the trace was generated. | • Root span's attributes mapped to `environment` |\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\n**Filtering by metadata key in Langfuse**\n\nLangfuse only supports filtering on top-level keys within the `metadata` of an event.\n\nBy default, all OpenTelemetry attributes and resource attributes are mapped into an `attributes` and `resourceAttributes` key within `metadata` and are thus not queryable.\n\nIf you want to query on specific attributes, you can use the `langfuse.trace.metadata` prefix to map them to the top-level `metadata` object of the trace.\nThe following snippet will produce a filterable `user_name` property in the `metadata` object of the trace:\n\n```python\nwith tracer.start_as_current_span(\"Langfuse Attributes\") as span:\n span.set_attribute(\"langfuse.trace.metadata.user_name\", \"user-123\")\n```\n\n</Callout>\n\n### Observation-Level Attributes [#observation-level-attributes]\n\nThese attributes are applied to individual observations (spans) within a trace ([data model](/docs/observability/data-model)).\n\n| Langfuse Field | Description | Mapped from OTel Attribute |\n| ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| <a id=\"type\"></a>`type` | The [type of observation](/docs/observability/features/observation-types). A recognized `langfuse.observation.type` always wins; see [ingestion transformations](#ingestion-transformations). | • `langfuse.observation.type`: `\"span\" \\| \"generation\" \\| \"event\" \\| \"embedding\" \\| \"agent\" \\| \"tool\" \\| \"chain\" \\| \"retriever\" \\| \"guardrail\" \\| \"evaluator\"`<br/>• If unset or unrecognized: inferred from other conventions, then from a model attribute (`generation`), then `\"span\"` |\n| <a id=\"level\"></a>`level` | The [severity level](/docs/observability/features/log-levels) of the observation. | • `langfuse.observation.level`: `\"DEBUG\" \\| \"DEFAULT\" \\| \"WARNING\" \\| \"ERROR\"`, default: `\"DEFAULT\"`<br/>• Inferred from `span.status.code` |\n| <a id=\"statusMessage\"></a>`statusMessage` | A message describing the status of the observation, often used for errors. | • `langfuse.observation.status_message`: `string`<br/>• Inferred from `span.status.message` |\n| <a id=\"obs-metadata\"></a>`metadata` | A flexible object for storing additional unstructured data. See note below. | • `langfuse.observation.metadata.*`: `string` |\n| <a id=\"obs-input\"></a>`input` | The input data for this specific observation. | • `langfuse.observation.input`: `(JSON) string`<br/>• `gen_ai.prompt`<br/>• `input.value` (OpenInference)<br/>• `mlflow.spanInputs` (MLFlow) |\n| <a id=\"obs-output\"></a>`output` | The output data from this specific observation. | • `langfuse.observation.output`: `(JSON) string`<br/>• `gen_ai.completion`<br/>• `output.value` (OpenInference)<br/>• `mlflow.spanOutputs` (MLFlow) |\n| <a id=\"model\"></a>`model` | The name of the generative model used. _Generation only._ | • `langfuse.observation.model.name`<br/>• `gen_ai.request.model`<br/>• `gen_ai.response.model`<br/>• `llm.model_name`<br/>• `model` |\n| <a id=\"modelParameters\"></a>`modelParameters` | Key-value pairs for model invocation settings. _Generation only._ | • `langfuse.observation.model.parameters`: `JSON string`<br/>• `gen_ai.request.*`<br/>• `llm.invocation_parameters.*` |\n| <a id=\"usage\"></a>`usage` | Token counts for the generation. _Generation only._ | • `langfuse.observation.usage_details`: `JSON string`<br/>• `gen_ai.usage.*`<br/>• `llm.token_count.*` |\n| <a id=\"cost\"></a>`cost` | The calculated cost in USD. _Generation only._ | • `langfuse.observation.cost_details`: `JSON string`<br/>• `gen_ai.usage.cost` (set as `total` key) |\n| <a id=\"prompt\"></a>`prompt` | The name of a versioned prompt managed in Langfuse. _Generation only._ | • `langfuse.observation.prompt.name`: `string`<br/>• `langfuse.observation.prompt.version`: `integer` |\n| <a id=\"completionStartTime\"></a>`completionStartTime` | Timestamp for when the model began generating. _Generation only._ | • `langfuse.observation.completion_start_time`: `ISO 8601 date string` |\n| <a id=\"obs-version\"></a>`version` | The [version](/docs/observability/features/releases-and-versioning) of the observation. | • `langfuse.version`: `string` |\n| <a id=\"obs-environment\"></a>`environment` | The deployment [environment](/docs/observability/features/environments) where the observation was generated. | • `langfuse.environment`<br/>• `deployment.environment`<br/>• `deployment.environment.name` |\n\n<Callout type=\"info\">\n**Filtering by metadata key in Langfuse**\n\nLangfuse only supports filtering on top-level keys within the `metadata` of an event.\n\nBy default, all OpenTelemetry attributes and resource attributes are mapped into an `attributes` and `resourceAttributes` key within `metadata` and are thus not queryable.\n\nIf you want to query on specific attributes, you can use the `langfuse.observation.metadata` prefix to map them to the top-level `metadata` object of the observation.\nThe following snippet will produce a filterable `user_name` property in the `metadata` object:\n\n```python\nwith tracer.start_as_current_span(\"Langfuse Attributes\") as span:\n span.set_attribute(\"langfuse.observation.metadata.user_name\", \"user-123\")\n```\n\n</Callout>\n\n### Ingestion transformations [#ingestion-transformations]\n\n Langfuse accepts incomplete or non-standard OTLP spans instead of rejecting\n them. The request still succeeds; the span is rewritten.\n\n1. **Accepted `langfuse.observation.type` values** are `span`, `generation`, `event`, `embedding`, `agent`, `tool`, `chain`, `retriever`, `guardrail`, and `evaluator`.\n2. **An unrecognized explicit type is not rejected.** A typo or a vendor-specific string such as `llm` falls through to other mapped conventions (for example `gen_ai.operation.name`), then to the model fallback, then to `span`.\n3. **A model attribute infers `generation` only as a fallback** — when no recognized `langfuse.observation.type` and no higher-priority convention applied. A valid explicit type always wins, even if the span also has a model name (`langfuse.observation.model.name`, `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.model`, `llm.model_name`, or `model`).\n4. **Missing timestamps are filled in.** If `startTimeUnixNano` or `endTimeUnixNano` is missing or unparseable, Langfuse copies the remaining edge so both start and end are set (the observation has zero duration). If both are missing, both become the ingest time. Send both fields on every span.\n\n## Next steps\n\nOnce spans are arriving in Langfuse, [Tracing in the Langfuse Academy](/academy/tracing) covers how traces are structured and which attributes make them useful downstream, and [Monitoring](/academy/monitoring) covers how to read them once they are there.\n\n## Troubleshooting\n\n- If you encounter `4xx` errors while self-hosting Langfuse, please upgrade your deployment to the latest version. The OpenTelemetry endpoint was first introduced in Langfuse [v3.22.0](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases/tag/v3.22.0) and has seen significant improvements since then.\n- Langfuse supports OTLP over HTTP with both `HTTP/JSON` and `HTTP/protobuf`. `gRPC` is not supported yet.\n- If an observation's type or timestamps look wrong, Langfuse may have rewritten them on ingest. See [Ingestion transformations](#ingestion-transformations).\n\n<!-- agent-instructions -->\n\n---\n\n## Agent Instructions\n\nThis page is part of the [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com) documentation, published as plain Markdown for AI agents. Every page is available as Markdown by appending `.md` to its URL, or by sending an `Accept: text/markdown` header. This page: `https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry.md`.\n\n### Querying these docs\n\nIf the answer is not on this page, query the documentation instead of guessing:\n\n- **Semantic search** across all Langfuse docs, returning an answer with the relevant pages and excerpts. Ask a specific, self-contained question:\n\n ```bash\n curl -sG \"https://langfuse.com/api/search-docs\" --data-urlencode \"query=How do I trace a LangGraph agent?\"\n ```\n\n- **Index of every page**: <https://langfuse.com/llms.txt>, with per-section indexes [llms-docs.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-docs.txt), [llms-integrations.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-integrations.txt), and [llms-self-hosting.txt](https://langfuse.com/llms-self-hosting.txt).\n\n### Before writing Langfuse code\n\n- **Install the [Langfuse Agent Skill](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/agent-skill).** It encodes Langfuse's own best practices for instrumentation, prompt management, and evaluation, and materially improves results.\n- **Read [What does a good trace look like?](https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/best-practices.md)** before instrumenting an application.\n- **Verify endpoints, parameters, and response fields** against the [API reference](https://api.reference.langfuse.com) instead of inferring them from code examples.\n- **Use the [Langfuse CLI](https://langfuse.com/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/cli)** (`npx langfuse-cli api <resource> <action>`) to read or write traces, prompts, datasets, and scores from the terminal.\n\nFound an error in these docs? Please open an issue at <https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs/issues>.\n"}

How SREs can utilize Langfuse

  • Instrument and segment traffic
    • Ingest traces to capture prompts, responses, token/cost, and latency: Get Started with Tracing https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
    • Use environments (prod/staging/dev) to isolate data and dashboards per deployment: Observability Overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
    • Propagate userId early for per-user cost/quality analytics: User Tracking https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users
      • Python example:
        • from langfuse import observe, propagate_attributes
        • @observe()
        • def handle(req): with propagate_attributes(user_id="user_123"): ...
  • Monitor reliability, quality, and spend
    • Custom dashboards for latency percentiles, cost, tokens, error levels, and score trends: Custom Dashboards https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
    • Turn any filtered table view into a chart, then “Add to dashboard”: Chart any table https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/events-table-charts
    • Set threshold alerts on metrics like cost, latency, and evaluation scores; notify Slack/webhooks/GitHub Actions: LLM Observability (alerts section) https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability and Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
    • Cost management best practices (monitors for provider spend vs. org spend alerts, sampling): LLM cost management https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/llm-cost-management
  • Integrate with on-call and incident workflows
    • Slack: connect once and route prompt-change and metric alerts to channels: Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
    • Webhooks for CI/CD or incident tools; HMAC signature verification included: Webhooks & Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/webhooks-slack-integrations
  • Close the loop with the AI team
    • Evaluate production quality continuously (online evaluation + user feedback), visualize in dashboards, and alert on regressions: LLM Observability & Monitoring https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability
    • Manage prompts like code with labels, CI gates, Slack notifications, and canary rollouts (90/10) so SREs can gate risky changes: Prompt CI/CD guide https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/prompt-cicd

Minimal, runnable setup snippets

  • JS/TS (OpenTelemetry + OpenAI tracing): Get Started https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
    • instrumentation.ts
      • import { NodeSDK } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-node"
      • import { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from "@langfuse/otel"
      • const sdk = new NodeSDK({ spanProcessors: [new LangfuseSpanProcessor()] })
      • sdk.start()
    • index.ts
      • import "./instrumentation"
    • Wrap OpenAI
      • import OpenAI from "openai"
      • import { observeOpenAI } from "@langfuse/openai"
      • const openai = observeOpenAI(new OpenAI())
      • await openai.chat.completions.create({ model: "gpt-4o", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hi" }] })
  • Python (user attribution)
    • from langfuse import observe, propagate_attributes
    • @observe()
    • def process(user_query): with propagate_attributes(user_id="user_123"): ...

How to integrate with your AI team’s workflow

  • Dev/instrumentation: add tracing in services and agents; adopt attribute propagation (userId, session) and meaningful trace/observation names. Best practices: Observability Overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
  • Quality gates: build datasets and evaluators; track live scores and alert on drops; surface poor user-rated traces to triage: LLM Observability https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability
  • Dashboards: one “Production Monitoring” dashboard (p95/p99 latency by model, error rate, cost by feature, score averages); a separate “Cost” dashboard for token and USD breakdowns: Custom Dashboards https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
  • On-call: route alerts to Slack/webhooks with clear thresholds and environments; link alerts back to filtered traces for fast root-cause analysis: Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
  • Prompt changes: use labels, run evaluations in CI, notify approvers in Slack, then canary and monitor live metrics before full rollout: Prompt CI/CD https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/prompt-cicd

One follow-up suggestion: Would you like a starter “Production Monitoring” dashboard and an example Slack alert configuration (latency and cost) tailored to your environments?

How SREs can utilize Langfuse

  • Instrument and segment traffic
    • Ingest traces to capture prompts, responses, token/cost, and latency: Get Started with Tracing https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
    • Use environments (prod/staging/dev) to isolate data and dashboards per deployment: Observability Overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
    • Propagate userId early for per-user cost/quality analytics: User Tracking https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users
      • Python example:
        • from langfuse import observe, propagate_attributes
        • @observe()
        • def handle(req): with propagate_attributes(user_id="user_123"): ...
  • Monitor reliability, quality, and spend
    • Custom dashboards for latency percentiles, cost, tokens, error levels, and score trends: Custom Dashboards https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
    • Turn any filtered table view into a chart, then “Add to dashboard”: Chart any table https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/events-table-charts
    • Set threshold alerts on metrics like cost, latency, and evaluation scores; notify Slack/webhooks/GitHub Actions: LLM Observability (alerts section) https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability and Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
    • Cost management best practices (monitors for provider spend vs. org spend alerts, sampling): LLM cost management https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/llm-cost-management
  • Integrate with on-call and incident workflows
    • Slack: connect once and route prompt-change and metric alerts to channels: Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
    • Webhooks for CI/CD or incident tools; HMAC signature verification included: Webhooks & Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/webhooks-slack-integrations
  • Close the loop with the AI team
    • Evaluate production quality continuously (online evaluation + user feedback), visualize in dashboards, and alert on regressions: LLM Observability & Monitoring https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability
    • Manage prompts like code with labels, CI gates, Slack notifications, and canary rollouts (90/10) so SREs can gate risky changes: Prompt CI/CD guide https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/prompt-cicd

Minimal, runnable setup snippets

  • JS/TS (OpenTelemetry + OpenAI tracing): Get Started https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
    • instrumentation.ts
      • import { NodeSDK } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-node"
      • import { LangfuseSpanProcessor } from "@langfuse/otel"
      • const sdk = new NodeSDK({ spanProcessors: [new LangfuseSpanProcessor()] })
      • sdk.start()
    • index.ts
      • import "./instrumentation"
    • Wrap OpenAI
      • import OpenAI from "openai"
      • import { observeOpenAI } from "@langfuse/openai"
      • const openai = observeOpenAI(new OpenAI())
      • await openai.chat.completions.create({ model: "gpt-4o", messages: [{ role: "user", content: "Hi" }] })
  • Python (user attribution)
    • from langfuse import observe, propagate_attributes
    • @observe()
    • def process(user_query): with propagate_attributes(user_id="user_123"): ...

How to integrate with your AI team’s workflow

  • Dev/instrumentation: add tracing in services and agents; adopt attribute propagation (userId, session) and meaningful trace/observation names. Best practices: Observability Overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
  • Quality gates: build datasets and evaluators; track live scores and alert on drops; surface poor user-rated traces to triage: LLM Observability https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability
  • Dashboards: one “Production Monitoring” dashboard (p95/p99 latency by model, error rate, cost by feature, score averages); a separate “Cost” dashboard for token and USD breakdowns: Custom Dashboards https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
  • On-call: route alerts to Slack/webhooks with clear thresholds and environments; link alerts back to filtered traces for fast root-cause analysis: Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
  • Prompt changes: use labels, run evaluations in CI, notify approvers in Slack, then canary and monitor live metrics before full rollout: Prompt CI/CD https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/prompt-cicd
