\"https://langfuse.com/self-hosting/upgrade/versioning\", \"title\": \"Versions & Compatibility\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nDatasets & experiments| Datasets only (experiments require Python SDK v4)| Datasets only (experiments require Python SDK v4) \\nPublic API & querying (`api.*`)| Supported| Unsupported (deprecated read APIs are removed on v4; upgrade to Python SDK v4) \\n \\nDeprecated.\\n **Limitations:**\\nCapability| OSS v2| OSS v3| OSS v4 \\n---|---|---|--- \\nTracing (legacy batch ingestion)| Supported| Supported| Unsupported \\nDatasets & experiments| Datasets only (experiments require Python SDK v4)| Datasets only (experiments require Python SDK v4)| Datasets only (experiments require Python SDK v4) \\nMedia (multimodal)| Requires OSS v3| Supported| Supported \\nPublic API & querying (`api.*`)| Supported| Supported| Unsupported (deprecated read APIs are removed on v4; upgrade to Python SDK v4) \\n \\nGA. Requires self-hosted server ≥ [3.63.0](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases/tag/v3.63.0); OSS v2 and older are unsupported.\\n **Limitations:**\\nCapability| OSS v3| OSS v4 \\n---|---|--- \\nTracing (OpenTelemetry)| Supported| Supported (real time with SDK ≥ 5.4.0) \\nPublic API & querying (`api.*`)| Use the [legacy APIs](/docs/api-and-data-platform/features/public-api#access-via-sdks) `api.legacy.observationsV1` / `api.legacy.metricsV1`| Supported (deprecated read APIs are removed on v4. Langfuse Cloud serves these endpoints until **November 16, 2026** (`2026-11-16`); migrate to v4 before this date.) \\n \\nDeprecated. Requires self-hosted server ≥ [3.63.0](https://github.com/langfuse/langfuse/releases/tag/v3.63.0); OSS v2 and older are unsupported.\\n **Limitations:**\\nCapability| OSS v3| OSS v4 \\n---|---|--- \\nTracing (OpenTelemetry)| Supported| Supported (data delayed up to 15 min; JS/TS SDK v5 ≥ 5.4.0 for real time) \"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/3997\", \"title\": \"Alerts and limits based on metrics (cost, evaluation, user-feedback), trigger webhook/email/slack/...\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: Alerts and limits based on metrics (cost, evaluation, user-feedback), trigger webhook/email/slack/...\\nCategory: Ideas\\nAuthor: @marcklingen\\nTimestamp: November 01, 2024\\nBody:\\n### Describe the feature or potential improvement\\n\\nSuggested by @chrisshaw [here](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1512#discussioncomment-9757098), as alerts are very distinct compared to [subscribing to new events](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1033)\\r\\n\\r\\n> Responding to events from individual scores, traces, etc seems fun but not urgent. In our case, we want to know that the moderation LLM app is still moderating correctly and want to be alerted based on an aggregation of scores crossing a threshold.\\r\\n>\\r\\n> Having looked at the linked concept, I wonder if this is really the answer. Not sure if this is what @hypernovas had in mind, but personally, what we're looking for is closer to getting alerted along a metric, not an event. Similar to hitting various thresholds in New Relic or Sentry.\\r\\n> \\r\\n> As a concrete example, suppose we're using a large language model to look for abusive behavior. We want to know that it's continuing to perform its task adequately as models and behaviors drift. So we set up an evaluation (let's say a model-based eval or a custom eval) that runs on our generations. Every individual trace's score is going to be variable, but we want to know if something is seriously wrong with our LLM app if it falls beneath a certain average score, aggregated over the last hour. That's when we want to get alerted (whether it's slack or general webhook is less important).\\n\\n### Additional information\\n\\n_No response_\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @Kleyt0n on May 24, 2025:\\n\\n I'm monitoring LLMs in production with Langfuse. It would be nice to have an alert feature (like a Slack connection) when the cost reaches a predefined limit.\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n Comment #2 from @gsvn on June 27, 2025:\\n\\n We have a similar setup & would be great to have alerts when a score goes below a certain average, aggregated over a configured period of time.\\r\\n\\r\\n> So we set up an evaluation (let's say a model-based eval or a custom eval) that runs on our generations. Every individual trace's score is going to be variable, but we want to know if something is seriously wrong with our LLM app if it falls beneath a certain average score, aggregated over the last hour.\\r\\n\\n\\n Comment #3 from @maxdeichmann on July 11, 2025:\\n\\n Hi all, we have a first webhook version out there: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started#webhooks\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know! Sending out webhooks on prompt versions is only the start. We will gradually increase the scope of the feature..\\n\\n Replies to comment #3:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #3 from maxdeichmann on September 04, 2025:\\n\\n @maxdeichmann the link is invalid now. Do you have an up to date link for prompt version webhooks?\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #3 from maxdeichmann on September 04, 2025:\\n\\n https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/webhooks-slack-integrations\\n\\n Comment #4 from @joshwand on February 18, 2026:\\n\\n This is critical for production monitoring, and is a blocker for adoption at one of my enterprise customers. \\n\\n Comment #5 from @marksalpeter on June 19, 2026:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n Hi everyone! Our new [Monitors](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/~/monitors) feature just shipped in cloud beta. You can set threshold alerts on metrics like cost, scores, and latency and route them to Slack, webhooks, or GitHub Actions ([docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/monitors)).\\n\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know.\\ncc: @Kleyt0n, @gsvn, @joshwand\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/11025\", \"title\": \"Ability to set alarms for metrics\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: Ability to set alarms for metrics\\nCategory: Ideas\\nAuthor: @Ravit436\\nTimestamp: December 10, 2025\\nBody:\\n### Describe the feature or potential improvement\\n\\nAbility to set alarms for metrics whenever a metric crosses a threshold based on the datapoints, in case of anomaly, etc.\\n\\n### Additional information\\n\\n_No response_\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @jannikmaierhoefer on December 11, 2025:\\n\\n Thanks @Ravit436! We are tracking this here: https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/3997\\n\\n Comment #2 from @marksalpeter on June 19, 2026:\\n\\n Hi @Ravit436! This just shipped as [Monitors](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/~/monitors). You get alerted whenever a metric crosses a threshold via Slack, webhooks, or Github Dispatch. ([docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/monitors)).\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know.\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"record_type\": \"site\", \"url\": \"https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/llm-cost-management\", \"title\": \"LLM cost management: how to track, attribute, and control spend - Langfuse\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n 1. **Threshold alerts on cost metrics.** In Langfuse, [monitors](/docs/metrics/features/monitors) evaluate a metric such as summed observation cost over a rolling window, filtered by model, tags, user, or environment, with warning and alert thresholds that notify via Slack, webhook, or GitHub Actions.\\n\\n---\\n\\n 2. **Hard budgets and rate limits.** Enforcement belongs in the request path, which is a gateway job: per-team budgets and key-level rate limits stop runaway spend rather than reporting it. Observability tells you what to set the limits to.\\n\\n---\\n\\n 3. **Controls on the observability bill itself.** Langfuse Cloud pricing is unit-based (traces + observations + scores), so [sampling](/docs/observability/features/sampling) and span filtering reduce that bill directly, and [spend alerts](/docs/administration/spend-alerts) notify org admins when the Langfuse Cloud bill itself crosses a threshold. Note the distinction: spend alerts cover what you pay Langfuse, monitors cover what you pay model providers.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Optimize once measurement is trustworthy\\nOptimization is the last layer for a reason: once cost data is accurate and attributed, the highest-spend segments show you where to start. The recurring levers:\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Route by task difficulty.** Group cost by model and feature to find high-volume, simple tasks running on premium models, then validate the cheaper model with an [evaluation setup](/resources/engineering/llm-evaluation-strategy) before switching.\\n\\n---\\n\\n * **Use prompt caching deliberately.** Providers discount cached input tokens; tracking cached tokens as their own priced bucket shows the realized savings per feature and whether your prompts are structured to hit the cache.\\n\\n---\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}, {\"type\": \"document\", \"github_discussion\", \"url\": \"https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1033\", \"title\": \"Subscribe to Langfuse Events via Webhooks\", \"source\": {\"content\": [{\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Title: Subscribe to Langfuse Events via Webhooks\\nCategory: Ideas\\nAuthor: @marcklingen\\nTimestamp: February 01, 2024\\nBody:\\nLangfuse produces many different events. For various reasons it can be useful to subscribe to them via a webhook.\\r\\n\\r\\nPotential events\\r\\n- score:create (user feedback, eval, ...)\\r\\n- trace:create\\r\\n- prompt:create\\r\\n\\r\\nVery early idea, raised by a couple of teams using Langfuse. Feel free to add your thoughts or what you'd like to see/contribute.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n-----\\r\\n**Edit**\\r\\n\\r\\nWe have a first webhook version out there: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompt-management/features/webhooks-slack-integrations\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know! Sending out webhooks on prompt versions is only the start. We will gradually increase the scope of the feature.\\r\\n\\r\\n----\\r\\n\\r\\n**Update - June 18th, 2026**\\r\\n\\r\\nOur new [Monitors](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/~/monitors) feature just shipped in cloud beta. As requested by many of you, alerts are triggered based on aggregated metrics over a sliding window. [Learn more in the docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/monitors).\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know.\\nComments:\\n\\n Comment #1 from @khareyash05 on February 02, 2024:\\n\\n Hey This feature will be very useful! Will this be a Slack Webhook Url or a Discord Webhook Url?\\n\\n Replies to comment #1:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #1 from khareyash05 on February 02, 2024:\\n\\n Currently thinking about generic webhook. It is easy to then setup a Slack workflow to consume this information and print to Slack or use Zapier/Make/n8n to build a quick custom consumer in order to pipe the events to other channels.\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #1 from khareyash05 on March 13, 2024:\\n\\n Hey another event I can think of is whenever a new member is added/removed to/from the project \\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nAlso with webhook url we can also send an email that this person was added to the workspace by this person.\\n\\n Comment #2 from @clemra on March 27, 2024:\\n\\n + 1 in #1512 \\n\\n Replies to comment #2:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #2 from clemra on March 27, 2024:\\n\\n Thanks! Curious what is the status for the webhook capability? Something we were looking at is based on the cost burst, LLM API outage or latency spikes, we can publish events. This can be very useful for LLM app ops for many orgs.\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #2 from clemra on April 29, 2024:\\n\\n We are waiting for v3 changes before adding webhook capabilities. Thereby these can happen behind async queues instead of having to be run within sync apis. More context on this here: https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1902\\n\\n Comment #3 from @chrisshaw on June 12, 2024:\\n\\n Sorry to bother twice, walking over from #1512 . Wanted to extend the [very good use cases we also have](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1033#discussioncomment-8933260) that @hypernovas brought up with what I shared in [my reply](https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1512#discussioncomment-9757098) in the prior discussion: alerts based on sliding window aggregated scores. Responding to events from _individual_ scores, traces, etc seems fun but not urgent. In our case, we want to know that the moderation LLM app is still moderating correctly and want to be alerted based on an aggregation of scores crossing a threshold.\\n\\n Replies to comment #3:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #3 from chrisshaw on November 01, 2024:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n thanks for the feedback and sorry for the slow response. I fully agree that alerts are very distinct from rule-based triggers on every newly created object in Langfuse. I create a new thread to track this independently: https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/3997\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #3 from chrisshaw on February 06, 2026:\\n\\n > alerts based on sliding window aggregated scores\\r\\n\\r\\n+1 for this need\\n\\n Comment #4 from @ajram23 on September 30, 2024:\\n\\n +1 please. \\n\\n Comment #5 from @arackley-tribal on October 22, 2024:\\n\\n +1 Would love to be able to use this to be notified when Langfuse is noticing errors in traces etc. \\n\\n Comment #6 from @barseghyanartur on November 21, 2024:\\n\\n Copied from https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/4342\\r\\n\\r\\n----\\r\\n\\r\\n**Feature request: Lifecycle hooks in LangFuse**\\r\\n\\r\\nIntroduce lifecycle hooks in LangFuse to trigger custom actions during key events (such as prompt promotion to production).\\r\\n\\r\\nThese hooks should provide flexibility, allowing integration with external systems via webhooks.\\r\\n\\r\\nInitial implementation could be as simple as managing that through the UI:\\r\\n\\r\\n- Event to hook into.\\r\\n- Webhook URL.\\r\\n- Configuration (security tokens, retries, timeouts).\\r\\n- Additional payload parameters.\\r\\n\\r\\nOn a long term, support for a reproducible configuration format for defining lifecycle hooks would be useful. Think of version-controlled deployments or \\\"manual\\\" environment duplications.\\r\\n\\r\\n----\\r\\n\\n\\n Replies to comment #6:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #6 from barseghyanartur on June 13, 2025:\\n\\n @barseghyanartur thanks a lot for sharing this! Can you maybe share a bit which events exactly would be helpful for you and what you would do with them?\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #6 from barseghyanartur on June 26, 2025:\\n\\n Thanks for getting back.\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nI'd love as many hookable events as possible, but these three are my highest priority:\\r\\n\\r\\n#### Prompt label created\\r\\n\\r\\n**Event**: Prompt label created. \\r\\nFires whenever a prompt receives a (new) label. For example, I have a suite of integration tests that should run whenever prompts change. I can define custom labels like `dev` or `qa` (in addition to `production`) and automatically verify that everything still works after an update.\\r\\n\\r\\n#### Prompt label removed\\r\\n\\r\\n**Event**: Prompt label removed. \\r\\nFires whenever an existing label is removed. If someone accidentally removed the `production` label, my integration tests will catch it immediately - preventive maintenance rules!\\r\\n\\r\\n> *I expect this to cover the case where a prompt itself is removed.*\\r\\n\\r\\n#### Prompt updated\\r\\n\\r\\n**Event**: Prompt updated. \\r\\nFires whenever the prompt text or its configuration changes. For instance, if someone tweaks the user- or system-prompt text or renames a variable, integration tests are executed.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #6 from barseghyanartur on June 27, 2025:\\n\\n Awesome, thanks so much. We have a PR for exactly these events and will launch this asap. I will keep you posted here.\\n\\n Comment #7 from @chai3 on December 16, 2024:\\n\\n datasets:create\\r\\nI want to run agent experiments(not prompt experiments)\\n\\n Replies to comment #7:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #7 from chai3 on August 01, 2025:\\n\\n Thanks\\r\\nhttps://langfuse.com/changelog/2025-07-24-remote-experiment-triggers\\n\\n Comment #8 from @camwardy on February 01, 2025:\\n\\n prompt:create would be really useful for our team - we'd like to store the names in our DB\\n\\n Replies to comment #8:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #8 from camwardy on June 13, 2025:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n @camwardy thanks a lot for the feedback! What exactly would be your workflow here if you had such a webhook?\\r\\n\\r\\nAs side note: you are able to configure refetching new prompts in the SDK ([docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started#caching-in-client-sdks)).\\n\\n Comment #9 from @george-bsq on February 05, 2025:\\n\\n +1 would be useful when the production label moves to a different version of the same prompt.\\n\\n Replies to comment #9:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #9 from george-bsq on February 10, 2025:\\n\\n thanks for sharing\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #9 from george-bsq on June 13, 2025:\\n\\n @george-bsq thanks a lot for the feedback! What exactly would be your workflow here if you had such a webhook?\\r\\n\\r\\nAs side note: you are able to configure refetching new prompts in the SDK ([docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started#caching-in-client-sdks)).\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #9 from george-bsq on June 17, 2025:\\n\\n @maxdeichmann Hi Max, thank you for showing interest in this.\\r\\n\\r\\nWhile I'd love to use Langfuse as my prompt manager, I'd prefer not to add another third-party dependency to my system, let alone one that my system initialization depends on. Given a hook like the one I described, I could use it to deploy the prompt to my own infrastructure whenever a new version is promoted to 'production'.\\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #9 from george-bsq on June 27, 2025:\\n\\n @george-bsq Awesome, thanks so much. We have a PR for exactly these events and will launch this asap. I will keep you posted here.\\n\\n Comment #10 from @mohamedgomran on February 18, 2025:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n `prompt:update` will also be useful, the langfuse SDK is caching the prompt in the the memory and we need a way to get notified when prompt changes so we can invalidate the cache\\n\\n Replies to comment #10:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #10 from mohamedgomran on March 08, 2025:\\n\\n Absolutely, that's why I ended up here. \\r\\nOur use case:\\r\\nWe are building a pretty elaborated AI agent (for dating :)) and we need a super low latency, with always up to date prompts in order for our product team to iterate as quickly as possible.\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #10 from mohamedgomran on March 10, 2025:\\n\\n > the langfuse SDK is caching the prompt in the the memory\\r\\n\\r\\nYou can configure the cache TTL. The SDK will deliver the stale prompt to optimize latency and revalidate in the background. By default, this occurs every minute. Does this not work for you?\\r\\n\\r\\nhttps://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started#caching-in-client-sdks\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #10 from mohamedgomran on March 10, 2025:\\n\\n Can confirm that this works for me and it really valuable. @lasryaric highly recommend it!\\n\\n Comment #11 from @AlmogBaku on March 18, 2025:\\n\\n any updates on that?\\n\\n Comment #12 from @lasryaric on March 18, 2025:\\n\\n A ttl is not enough because I want to have caching for the prompts (they\\r\\ntake up to 300ms to fetch) but I also want to be able to deploy new prompts\\r\\ninstantly by invalidating my cache. Hence the need for the webhook.\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\nOn Tue, Mar 18, 2025 at 9:54 AM Almog Baku ***@***.***> wrote:\\r\\n\\r\\n> any updates on that?\\r\\n>\\r\\n> —\\r\\n> Reply to this email directly, view it on GitHub\\r\\n> <https://github.com/orgs/langfuse/discussions/1033#discussioncomment-12535394>,\\r\\n> or unsubscribe\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"> <https://github.com/notifications/unsubscribe-auth/AACXUNPEEIQPEPQL5NORPTT2U7NN3AVCNFSM6AAAAABCVNXDZOVHI2DSMVQWIX3LMV43URDJONRXK43TNFXW4Q3PNVWWK3TUHMYTENJTGUZTSNA>\\r\\n> .\\r\\n> You are receiving this because you were mentioned.Message ID:\\r\\n> ***@***.***>\\r\\n>\\r\\n\\r\\n\\r\\n-- \\r\\nAric Lasry\\r\\n+33 7 49 50 55 74\\r\\n\\n\\n Comment #13 from @agbragin on May 26, 2025:\\n\\n +1 `trace:create` and `score:create` would be extremely useful for automatic triggering of custom evaluation pipelines.\\r\\n\\n\\n Replies to comment #13:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #13 from agbragin on June 13, 2025:\\n\\n Hi @agbragin thanks a lot for sharing this! What is the use-case for this? Does the open-sourcing of LLM as a judge in Langfuse help you here to run evals async?\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #13 from agbragin on June 16, 2025:\\n\\n Hi! Thanks for the response! I would say that open-sourcing of LLM-as-a-judge would _not_ solve the issue. \\r\\n\\r\\nThe use case is to evaluate traces (including the complex ones, e.g. agentic) on arrival using all kinds of evaluation (functional, heuristics-based, gold comparison).\\r\\n\\r\\n`score:create` can be used to push notification when scores are out of the desired range.\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #13 from agbragin on June 26, 2025:\\n\\n same here. @maxdeichmann \\r\\n1. Our local host LLM can't support structure output and langfuse evalutor couldn't work. `trace:create` can help this.\\r\\n2. Evaluation might need processing in advance. E.g: trajectory evaluation and using metadata to help understand the task.\\r\\n3. `score:create` help push notification.\\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #13 from agbragin on June 27, 2025:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \" @agbragin + @Haoping-Xiao: we thought to also have `score-create` and `trace-create` events. Yet, if your application has very high load, this would also mean that we push out many webhooks to your systems. Would you be willing to deal with this load or would you like to have some sort of sampling / rate limiting?\\n\\n Reply #5 to comment #13 from agbragin on June 29, 2025:\\n\\n I think a general rate limiting is convenient. In addition, filter settings for traces/scores[threshold settings] are also helpful to reduce the load.\\n\\n Reply #6 to comment #13 from agbragin on June 30, 2025:\\n\\n @marcklingen Currently rate limiting is not critical for us – the idea is to configure triggers for selected projects only (offline evaluation).\\n\\n Comment #14 from @maxdeichmann on June 13, 2025:\\n\\n Hi everyone,\\r\\n\\r\\nwe are currently actively looking into this feature! I would love to learn a bit more which use-cases might be helpful here. So far I think most requested are alerting based on aggregates (e.g. score value hits threshold over time) or webhooks once prompts change (e.g. new version / label). Do you have any other use cases?\\r\\n\\r\\nIf yes, tell me more about what data you need to run your workflows and I will happily consider that.\\n\\n Replies to comment #14:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #14 from maxdeichmann on June 14, 2025:\\n\\n **I'm very much looking forward to this feature!**\\r\\n\\r\\nI can see myself using it for reporting exceptions.\\r\\nHowever, what I was missing for using Langfuse for that was:\\r\\n\\r\\n- the ability to turn off the automatic error level setting (as this interferes with manual settings).\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"- the ability to set error levels at trace level and not just observation level.\\r\\n- more or customisable level tags to allow more granular control over this.\\r\\n\\r\\nThen I think this could be really useful as a webhook to report errors to Slack, for example.\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #14 from maxdeichmann on June 16, 2025:\\n\\n Here are my basic cases 1. If a run fails, I'd like to log a GitHub ticket 2. If the score is under a certain value I'd like to log a ticket.\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #14 from maxdeichmann on June 23, 2025:\\n\\n We use webhooks to update a cache of the prompts in a KV connected to our serverless backend (sdk caching doesn't work because it's a new instance every time). This is something we need to switch to langfuse. \\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #14 from maxdeichmann on June 24, 2025:\\n\\n Hello, we're excited for this feature as well. In addition to the needs that many others have surfaced, we'd also like webhooks for when a metric defined on a dashboard falls below some threshold. We're specifically looking to do alerting if an Eval falls below a threshold.\\n\\n Reply #5 to comment #14 from maxdeichmann on June 27, 2025:\\n\\n - Our local host LLM can't support structure output and langfuse evalutor couldn't work. Can we trigger a `eval:create` signal when a custom evaluation pipeline setup is statisfied? This would be phenomenal. Otherwise, a `trace:create` signal that with some filters is great as well. `eval:create` can help manage the eval config while `trace:create` is not intuitive.\\r\\n- Evaluation might need processing in advance. E.g: trajectory evaluation and using metadata to help understand the task.\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"Currently the process is manual and a lot of responsibility is put on a single colleague who presses the \\\"production\\\" button in Langfuse. The button press impacts production directly without having a automated quality gate/process.\\n\\n Comment #17 from @maxdeichmann on July 11, 2025:\\n\\n Hi all, we have a first webhook version out there: https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started#webhooks\\r\\n\\r\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know! Sending out webhooks on prompt versions is only the start. We will gradually increase the scope of the feature.\\n\\n Replies to comment #17:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #17 from maxdeichmann on July 11, 2025:\\n\\n awesome!\\r\\nfew feedback/questions:\\r\\n- I see only a single option for `Name` in the filter. I guess there is a plan to add more columns like `Tags`, `Labels` etc?\\r\\n- Could you also add a feature to be able to customize webhook payload? I tried to integrate it with Slack Webhook API, but was not able to as there was no way to customize webhook payload to make it conform the schema Slack expects. \\r\\n - I understand it can be handled if we had our own webhook handler but would ideally be better if there is a direct way to achieve the same.\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #17 from maxdeichmann on July 12, 2025:\\n\\n Hi @kyu-aurelian, thanks a lot for the feedback.\\r\\n\\r\\n- For the filters: yes, we could add more. What exactly would you need them for?\\r\\n- Adjusting the payload: yes this would be great but I fear that this would make things complicated in the UI. We will for sure add a native slack integration.\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #17 from maxdeichmann on July 12, 2025:\\n\\n for filters, i would like to be notified on label changes (e.g. if a newer version of prompt is promoted to prod by having production label).\\r\\nwe basically want to be notified when there are changes that can affect production environment. \\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"and yes. it doesn't have to be supporting custom payload. if native slack integration can be supported that would be great!\\r\\nfwiw, I have seen a few services use `https://www.svix.com/` for their webhook integrations, which I thought was quite convenient. \\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #17 from maxdeichmann on August 03, 2025:\\n\\n @maxdeichmann I see that the current Prompt webhook code doesn't lay an infrastructue for additional event support - is this something worth checking out myself or are you guys in the middle of implementation and it's worth waiting for the next phase before extending it with my use case (evaluation score alerts)?\\n\\n Reply #5 to comment #17 from maxdeichmann on August 06, 2025:\\n\\n Hi @vardior9 thanks a lot for raising this question. We have this on our road map. However, as you noticed, we do not have the infra yet to support score based alerts. As this is extremely core to our infra, we will build this within our team as we know best which usage patterns of clickhouse will work.\\n\\n Comment #18 from @paolotamag on July 24, 2025:\\n\\n can this be used to alert us on slack when langfuse traces are failing (LEVEL : ERROR)?\\n\\n Comment #19 from @vaibhav3002 on August 06, 2025:\\n\\n @marcklingen - Hello, could you please tell the availability of the event subscription support via webhooks for scores as well?\\n\\n Comment #20 from @maxdeichmann on August 07, 2025:\\n\\n Hi all,\\r\\n\\r\\nthanks so much for the interest in Langfuse and sharing your needs here! \\r\\n\\r\\nWe launched the slack integration for prompt events recently (https://langfuse.com/changelog/2025-07-30-slack-prompt-notifications).\\r\\n\\r\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\nI know that many of you want to have tracing based alerts (e.g. score values, cost, latencies..) for these integrations. We have this very high up on our roadmap. We need to complete some more infrastructure work in the background to enable such alerts at scale unfortunately.\\n\\n Comment #21 from @amansr09 on September 19, 2025:\\n\\n \\r\\nWe are using LLM-as-a-Judge for automated evaluations and need to be alerted in real-time if a trace evaluation is incorrect, as manually checking the UI is not scalable for our production pipeline. can we get a new webhook event that triggers when an evaluation score falls below a set threshold would be a great solution, allowing us to send an immediate Slack notification and investigate.\\n\\n Replies to comment #21:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #21 from amansr09 on January 21, 2026:\\n\\n +1\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #21 from amansr09 on February 04, 2026:\\n\\n Hi @marcklingen - this is something we would love seeing as well. Webhooks when eval job is completed / failed. Let us know if this is already being built\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #21 from amansr09 on May 07, 2026:\\n\\n +1\\n\\n Comment #22 from @jkryanchou on November 02, 2025:\\n\\n I need a webhook or any other subscribed way to trigger next action. like trigger a webhook notification or call the n8n workflow.\\n\\n Comment #23 from @BrendanRitter on December 10, 2025:\\n\\n Our team is using langfuse for catching eval failures and doing x% general review. It would be great if you could tie a annotation queue to alerting so we knew when items have been added to those queues.\\n\\n Comment #24 from @manuel-reil on January 29, 2026:\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n We want to track token consumption, cost via openmeter.io for billing purposes. So webhook for the respected events would be good.\\n\\n Comment #25 from @ahmed-moubtahij on February 06, 2026:\\n\\n +1 to alerts on trace latency and +1 to alerts on sliding window aggregated eval scores\\n\\n Replies to comment #25:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #25 from ahmed-moubtahij on March 05, 2026:\\n\\n Very important to us too\\r\\n\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #25 from ahmed-moubtahij on March 17, 2026:\\n\\n important to us too\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #25 from ahmed-moubtahij on April 02, 2026:\\n\\n same here!\\r\\n\\n\\n Reply #4 to comment #25 from ahmed-moubtahij on April 13, 2026:\\n\\n Same\\n\\n Reply #5 to comment #25 from ahmed-moubtahij on April 24, 2026:\\n\\n Same\\n\\n Comment #26 from @musaabhasan on May 08, 2026:\\n\\n For webhooks tied to traces, scores, prompts, and annotation queues, I would design for replay and idempotency from the start. These events often drive downstream incident workflows, billing, or evaluation review, so duplicate delivery should be safe and missed delivery should be recoverable.\\n\\nFields I would want in each webhook envelope:\\n\\n- event_id, event_type, event_version\\n- project_id and environment\\n- resource_type and resource_id\\n- created_at and emitted_at\\n- trace_id / observation_id / prompt_version where relevant\\n- actor type, if available, without exposing unnecessary user data\\n- signature header and timestamp for verification\\n- delivery attempt number\\n\\nFor eval/annotation workflows, it would also help to include threshold context: score name, score value, threshold, baseline window, and reason the event fired. That lets teams route “latency regression”, “faithfulness regression”, and “human review queue item created” differently instead of treating every webhook as a generic notification.\\n\"}, {\"type\": \"text\", \"text\": \"\\n Comment #27 from @marksalpeter on June 19, 2026:\\n\\n Hi everyone! Our new [Monitors](https://cloud.langfuse.com/project/~/monitors) feature just shipped in cloud beta. You can set threshold alerts on metrics like cost, scores, and latency and route them to Slack, webhooks, or GitHub Actions ([docs](https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/monitors)).\\n\\nIf you have any questions or feedback, please let us know.\\n\\ncc: @hypernovas, @chrisshaw, @arackley-tribal, @jcbmllgn, @paolotamag, @vardior9, @amansr09, @ahmed-moubtahij, @manuel-reil, @howdymatt, @GNamDor, @marco-kalipso, @bostrt, @tswann\\n\\n Replies to comment #27:\\n\\n Reply #1 to comment #27 from marksalpeter on June 19, 2026:\\n\\n Thank you! We will definitely be trying this\\n\\n Reply #2 to comment #27 from marksalpeter on June 19, 2026:\\n\\n YES!\\n\\n Reply #3 to comment #27 from marksalpeter on June 22, 2026:\\n\\n Thanks for this feature!\\r\\n\\r\\nI tried the monitoring feature just a moment ago, and it was very useful for my usecase.\\r\\n\\r\\nI'm looking forward to seeing in production release.\\r\\n\\r\\nDo you have an estimated timeline for when it will be available in the self-hosted production release?\\n\"}], \"type\": \"content\"}}]}"}

    Sorry about that—here’s the answer.

    How SREs can utilize Langfuse

    • Instrument and segment traffic
      • Ingest traces to capture prompts, responses, token/cost, and latency: Get Started with Tracing https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/get-started
      • Use environments (prod/staging/dev) to isolate data and dashboards per deployment: Observability Overview https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/overview
      • Propagate userId early for per-user cost/quality analytics: User Tracking https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/users
        • Python example:
          • from langfuse import observe, propagate_attributes
          • @observe()
          • def handle(req): with propagate_attributes(user_id="user_123"): ...
    • Monitor reliability, quality, and spend
      • Custom dashboards for latency percentiles, cost, tokens, error levels, and score trends: Custom Dashboards https://langfuse.com/docs/metrics/features/custom-dashboards
      • Turn any filtered table view into a chart, then “Add to dashboard”: Chart any table https://langfuse.com/docs/observability/features/events-table-charts
      • Set threshold alerts on metrics like cost, latency, and evaluation scores; notify Slack/webhooks/GitHub Actions: LLM Observability (alerts section) https://langfuse.com/faq/all/llm-observability and Slack Integration https://langfuse.com/integrations/other/slack
      • Cost management best practices (monitors for provider spend vs. org spend alerts, sampling): LLM cost management https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/llm-cost-management
    • Integrate with on-call and incident workflows

    • Prompt changes: use labels, run evaluations in CI, notify approvers in Slack, then canary and monitor live metrics before full rollout: Prompt CI/CD https://langfuse.com/resources/engineering/prompt-cicd
